Create an interactive parliament chart

Source: R/parliamant_chart.R
parliament_chart.Rd

Draws the seats of an assembly as a hemicycle: one dot per seat, the parties forming wedges from left to right in the order of the data (or by size, see sort). A dashed line marks the majority, and the centre shows the total number of seats. Rows with the same party are added up.

Usage

parliament_chart(
  data,
  categorical_column,
  numerical_column,
  seat_size = NULL,
  padding = NULL,
  max_rows = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  title_font_size = 20,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bg_col = "white",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  subtitle_font_size = 13,
  fill = NULL,
  color_category = NULL,
  previous = NULL,
  majority = TRUE,
  coalition = NULL,
  coalition_builder = TRUE,
  regroup = TRUE,
  sort = c("none", "descending", "ascending"),
  arc = 180,
  inner_radius = 0.4,
  seat_shape = c("circle", "square"),
  center_label = "seats",
  legend = TRUE,
  tooltip = TRUE,
  animate = TRUE,
  axis_col = "#333333"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per party (rows with the same party are added up).

categorical_column

The name of the column giving the parties.

numerical_column

The name of the column giving the number of seats (whole numbers; other numbers are rounded with a warning).

seat_size

Optional. The diameter of the seats in pixels. By default the seats are as large as the chart allows. When the seats do not fit, they are made smaller.

padding

Optional. The space between two seats, in pixels. By default a fifth of the space given to each seat.

max_rows

Optional. The number of rows of seats. By default the number of rows that gives the largest seats.

title

Optional. The title of the chart.

title_font_size

The font size of the title. Defaults to 20.

font

The font family. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bg_col

The background colour. Defaults to "white".

width

Optional. The width of the chart.

height

Optional. The height of the chart.

subtitle

Optional. A subtitle under the title.

subtitle_font_size

The font size of the subtitle. Defaults to 13.

fill

Optional. The colours of the parties: one colour per party (recycled, in the order of the data), or a named vector mapping colours to parties (for instance c(Greens = "#3ca951")); the other parties get the ddplot palette.

color_category

Optional. The name of a D3 categorical colour scheme, such as "Tableau10" or "Set2", used when fill is not given.

previous

Optional. The name of a column giving the seats of each party at the previous election: the gains and losses are then shown in the legend and the tooltips.

majority

The seats needed for a majority: TRUE (default) for more than half of the seats, a number of seats, a share of the seats (a number below 1, such as 2/3, rounded up), or FALSE to draw no majority line.

coalition

Optional. A character vector of parties that form the coalition when the chart is first drawn.

coalition_builder

Logical. Let the viewer build a coalition by clicking parties, with a gauge under the hemicycle. Defaults to TRUE.

regroup

Logical. Move the seats of the coalition to the left of the hemicycle. Defaults to TRUE.

sort

The order of the parties from left to right: "none" (default, the order of the data or of the factor levels, as parties are usually ordered by political orientation), "descending" (largest first) or "ascending".

arc

The angle covered by the seats, in degrees, from 180 (default, a hemicycle) to 360 (a full ring).

inner_radius

The radius of the empty centre, as a fraction of the outer radius. Defaults to 0.4.

seat_shape

The shape of the seats: "circle" (default) or "square".

center_label

The text under the number of seats in the centre. Defaults to "seats"; FALSE leaves the centre empty.

legend

Logical. Show the legend, with the seats and shares (on the right when there is room, otherwise below). Defaults to TRUE.

tooltip

Logical. Show a tooltip when hovering the seats. Defaults to TRUE.

animate

Logical. Fill the seats from left to right when the chart comes into view. Defaults to TRUE.

axis_col

The colour of the texts. Defaults to "#333333".

Value

An interactive parliament chart (an r2d3 htmlwidget).

Details

The chart is also a coalition builder: click parties to put them together. Their seats gather on the left of the hemicycle, so the coalition has a majority when its seats cross the majority line, and a gauge under the hemicycle counts its seats.

Interactions

  • Hover a seat or a legend entry to highlight the party and see its seats, its share, its rank and how far it is from a majority (and its gains or losses with previous).

  • Click a seat or a legend entry (or press Enter on a focused legend entry) to add the party to the coalition, or to take it out. The coalition seats move to the left (see regroup), the gauge shows whether they reach the majority, and "Clear" empties the coalition.

Shiny

Inside Shiny, with r2d3::d3Output("id") and r2d3::renderD3(), clicking a party sets input$id_clicked to its name, and every change of the coalition sets input$id_coalition to a list with parties (a list of names: use unlist() to get a vector), seats, majority (the seats needed) and hasMajority. The coalition is kept when the chart is re-rendered (and input$id_coalition is updated if its seats changed), and the seats move smoothly to their new places when the results change.

Examples

political_results_example <- data.frame(
  political_party = c("SDP", "CDU", "Linke"),
  number_of_seats = c(200, 40, 30)
)
parliament_chart(
  data = political_results_example,
  categorical_column = "political_party",
  numerical_column = "number_of_seats",
  title = "An assembly of 270 seats"
)



# A toy assembly with party colours, the previous results and a coalition
assembly <- data.frame(
  party = c("Left", "Greens", "Social Democrats", "Liberals",
            "Conservatives", "Nationalists"),
  seats = c(28, 41, 152, 63, 187, 79),
  seats_before = c(39, 30, 171, 48, 170, 92)
)
parliament_chart(
  assembly, "party", "seats",
  previous = "seats_before",
  fill = c("#c0392b", "#3ca951", "#ff725c", "#efb118", "#4269d0", "#6b4e9c"),
  coalition = c("Social Democrats", "Greens", "Liberals"),
  title = "Who can govern?",
  subtitle = "Click the parties to build a coalition"
)
